title: Chapter 9
content:
"Are you alright?"

The guard materialized before him, his face lined with concern. Jakyeong nodded, squeezing out an apologetic smile. Moments earlier, he had deliberately tipped over a massive vase near the window, slicing his hand on a sharp edge while attempting to clear the mess. The guard had bolted up the stairs almost instantaneously.

To arrive so fast without a frantic call for help meant one thing: the house wasn't just being recorded on closed-circuit television—it was being monitored in real time. Which meant Jakyeong was operating on a leash, with zero room for reckless moves.

"Please wait here, sir. I’ll fetch the first-aid kit."

"Could you just grab me a bandage, please?"

Jakyeong yanked a few tissues from a box and pressed them tightly against the cut. The guard immediately summoned a maid over his radio to clear the shattered porcelain from the reception lounge, carefully transferring the flowers Kang Il-hyun had given him into a fresh vase. Taking the bandage from the guard, Jakyeong wrapped his palm. As the servant methodically swept up the remaining shards, Jakyeong drifted out into the hallway, casually scouting the perimeter.

Since no other guards rushed out to intercept him, wandering the corridors seemed within acceptable bounds. To execute his assignment smoothly, he needed to lay out a mental blueprint of the estate, but its sheer size made reconnaissance exhausting. Worse, every single door featured an electronic deadbolt; entering without an encrypted keycard was out of the question.

He paced back and forth from one end of the hall to the other, pretending to admire the artwork lining the walls. Surprisingly, the paintings leaned toward warm, inviting tones—a stark, almost comical contrast to the master of the house.

Descending to the ground floor, he found the central hall hushed and empty, likely during a staff break. He circled the first-floor living room before stopping in front of a sprawling, floor-to-ceiling glass panel. Outside, the sun was dipping below the horizon, bathing the grounds in a striking crimson glow. Jakyeong perched himself on the wide window ledge, gazing out at the twilight, when faint footsteps rustled behind him.

He turned his head. The elderly housekeeper was approaching, her movement silent. Though her hair was silvered by age, her posture remained remarkably erect, and the soft crow's feet framing her eyes gave her a warm, approachable presence.

"It's a breathtaking view, isn't it?" she remarked gently. "Director Kang often stands right here to look out at the grounds."

"It really is," Jakyeong replied, keeping his voice light. "Though staying cooped up inside all day does get a bit boring."

"Oh, dear. It's a shame Young Master Seok-joo couldn't make it today."

"Seok-joo...?"

"The youngest master of the household. He's scheduled to arrive tomorrow morning."

Ah. The name clicked. Kang Il-hyun had mentioned inviting him over, claiming he'd keep Jakyeong company. What kind of person was he? Could he be the anonymous client who hired the hit? The sudden prospect of meeting one of the prime suspects sparked a subtle surge of excitement in Jakyeong's chest.

Suppressing the thought, he smoothly steered the conversation away. "Who designed this place?"

"A world-renowned architect built it," she said, pride lacing her tone. "Though Director Kang drafted the master blueprints himself."

"He designed it himself? Wow... impressive."

"He's a man of endless talents. There isn't a thing he cannot do."

She spoke of Kang Il-hyun as if he were an omnipotent deity. Jakyeong swallowed a smirk. Endless talents? I bet he can't come back from the dead. Time would tell soon enough.

"What was the architect's name?" Jakyeong asked casually.

"Why do you ask?"

"I really love the layout... I was thinking I'd like to meet him someday and commission a place just like it."

"Hmm... I believe he moved abroad right after construction finished. I'm not entirely sure where he went, though."

Moved abroad? More like moved six feet under. There was no way Il-hyun would leave the architect of his fortified mansion alive to sell the schematics. Capitalizing on her open mood, Jakyeong pressed a little further.

"I noticed there's a basement level in the elevator. What's down there?"

"Goodness, I wouldn't know. I've never been permitted down there myself."

"I see." Jakyeong let out a faint, disappointed sigh.

The old woman offered a sympathetic smile. "Why not ask Director Kang directly, Young Master Yi-an? I'm sure he'd tell you."

Jakyeong merely smiled back. Sure, if I want to trigger every red flag in his head. He had asked, but gained zero actionable intel. Before he could probe any further, the housekeeper excused herself, mentioning it was time to prepare dinner, and retreated toward the kitchen.

Left alone, Jakyeong swung both legs up onto the wide window frame, crossing them as he leaned back against the glass.

The sun sank deeper behind the distant mountain ridge, deepening the sky from burnt orange to a heavy, bruised violet. Whenever he was off-duty back home, he used to surf along the coast, floating idly on his board just to watch the sunset over the ocean. Sometimes, mesmerized by the deep red drowning in the waves, he used to imagine himself being dragged down into the abyss along with it.

Perhaps he had spaced out a bit too much this time, because he only registered the presence behind him when it was already too close. He turned his head to check—only to find a man's face resting barely an inch over his shoulder.

In pure, unadulterated shock, Jakyeong blurted out at top volume:

"Ah, ssibal—fuck!"

At a distance of less than a palm's length, Kang Il-hyun tilted his head naturally, his dark eyes locking onto Jakyeong's frantic ones.

Fuck?

"My," Il-hyun drawled, a dark glint in his eyes. "You certainly swear with remarkable flair."

Jakyeong’s brain short-circuited. He stammered frantically, "Th-That's... well... my mother was Korean, so..."

It was a profoundly stupid excuse. Yet, Il-hyun merely let out a low chuckle. Having approached without making a single sound, he hopped up onto the opposite side of the wide window frame, resting his weight effortlessly as he stared down at Jakyeong.

A cold stiffness crept up Jakyeong's neck. Did I blow my cover just now? Forcing his eyes to soften, he pushed his thick horn-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose and cast his gaze downward in an act of meek submission.

He peeked through his lashes, but Il-hyun remained silent. Unable to endure the suffocating pressure, Jakyeong lifted his head and offered a painfully awkward, timid smile.

"I'm... I'm so sorry. You just startled me..."

"Your hand."

"Pardon?"

Unsure of what he meant, Jakyeong blinked. Il-hyun extended his own hand first—long, elegant, and perfectly manicured fingers that matched their owner's sharp demeanor. Jakyeong stared at the open palm.

"Give me your hand."

"..."

Before Jakyeong could pull back, Il-hyun casually reached out and took his right hand, flipping it over to inspect the fresh bandage covering his palm.

"Fortunately, it doesn't look too deep."

Ah. He was checking the injury.

"Did... did the guards tell you?"

"It was one of my favorite vases," Il-hyun murmured, "but I won't hold you liable for the damage."

A favorite vase? How much could a piece of porcelain cost? Ten thousand dollars?

"No, I should compensate you for it," Jakyeong insisted softly.

"For seven hundred million won?"

"..."

"I mean, if you insist on paying me $500,000, I won't stop you."

Jakyeong froze, blinking in stunned silence. Five hundred thousand dollars for a vase? Judging by Il-hyun's unblinking expression, he wasn't joking. Holy shit. No wonder the guard had sprinted up the stairs like his life depended on it. It wasn't concern for a guest; the staff was terrified the house was being dismantled.

"I'm... I'm so sorry... I had no idea it was that expensive..."

The promise to pay died instantly in his throat. Fine. I'll compensate you by making your death completely painless. I won't put a bullet hole in that pretty face of yours. Whether he could actually keep that promise was a different story entirely.

Oblivious to the lethal calculations running behind those innocent glasses, Il-hyun simply let out a quiet laugh and dropped the topic. He turned his gaze toward the window instead. The last dying rays of daylight were surrendering to the horizon.

As shadows stretched across the room, darkness settled over Il-hyun's features. The shifting light carved sharp, striking angles into his face, giving him the sleek, terrifying aura of a predator poised for a hunt. Even man-to-man, Jakyeong had to admit the bastard was dangerously attractive.

As Jakyeong lost himself in thought, Il-hyun’s gaze shifted back from the glass, locking onto his face.

"It seems you'll be dining alone on your first night here. I have an evening engagement."

He slid off the window frame, standing up to his full height. Though his tone carried a smooth note of regret about not seeing each other until tomorrow, Jakyeong was secretly thrilled. Staying as far away from this man as possible was his top priority. Acting like a fragile, naive young master was proving infinitely more exhausting than snapping a man's neck.

Locking himself in the bathroom, Jakyeong climbed into the dry porcelain bathtub and pulled his laptop from his bag. Powering it on, he detached the right arm of his horn-rimmed glasses. The temple piece snapped off cleanly, transforming into a compact USB drive, which he inserted into his laptop. A series of media files immediately populated the screen.

The files contained high-resolution video feeds recorded during his walk through the estate. Scrubbing through the footage, he found the segment featuring Kang Il-hyun standing by the living room window. He hit pause. On screen, Il-hyun's quiet smile looked impossibly sharp—like a magazine cover model. It gave Jakyeong a petty flash of bruised ego.

Pushing aside the unexpected annoyance, Jakyeong fast-forwarded a few seconds, isolating a crystal-clear frame of Il-hyun's hands. He extracted the high-res image and encrypted it before transmitting it directly to Wang Han.

While waiting for the upload confirmation, Jakyeong leaned in, studying the palm lines visible on Il-hyun's hands.

Last year in Thailand, a Korean contact had taught him the basics of palmistry. Examining the high-definition image, he noticed Il-hyun's lifeline was absurdly long and deep, extending all the way down to his wrist. Unless someone actively murdered him, the bastard looked destined to live a thousand years.

Jakyeong glanced down at his own right palm. His own lifeline cut off abruptly right in the middle. Even palm lines are unfair in this damn world.

Plucking his e-cigarette from his pocket, he slid down into the tub, exhaling a thin stream of vapor toward the ceiling. Before the cloud could disperse, his encrypted phone vibrated against his thigh. He popped in his earpiece and hit answer.

Wang Han's voice filtered through the line.

[Got the image. Sharp quality.]

"How long to synthesize the biometric overlay?" Jakyeong asked.

[Even if I rush the lab tech right now? A week.]

To bypass the high-security deadbolts or access the restricted basement level, he needed Kang Il-hyun's precise fingerprints. While lifting residual prints from a surface was an option, high-resolution optical reconstruction was far more reliable. But a week was too long—variables could shift at any moment. He needed to locate the hidden safe and verify its contents as soon as humanly possible.

"Can't you push them to do it faster?"

[I'll see what I can do. Need anything else on your end?]

Jakyeong paused, then shook his head. "No. Nothing for now."

[Stay safe out there.]

"Yeah. You too, Hyung."

Ending the call, Jakyeong rested the laptop on his chest and stretched out inside the empty tub as if it were a bed. His long legs dangled awkwardly over the porcelain rim, but he didn't care, taking slow, rhythmic drags from his e-cigarette.

Above him, the oversized exhaust fan hummed quietly, greedily sucking up every trace of white vapor as fast as he produced it. Well, Jakyeong thought dryly, eyeing the vent, at least the ventilation in this deathtrap is world-class.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • 700 Million Won (7억): 700,000,000 KRW is equivalent to roughly $500,000 - $530,000 USD. Il-hyun casually tossing out this figure highlights his absurd wealth and sets up Jakyeong's silent panic over ruining an artifact worth half a million dollars.

  • Korean Swearing / "Ssibal" (씨발): Ssibal is one of the most common and versatile expletives in the Korean language (equivalent to "fuck" or "shit"). Jakyeong breaking his meek, polite persona by barking this out in extreme panic almost blows his cover immediately.

  • Palmistry / Lifeline (손금 / 생명줄): In East Asian palm reading, a long, clear lifeline extending down toward the wrist signifies longevity and vitality, while a broken or interrupted line suggests a short life or severe life-altering crises—a bitter irony given Jakyeong's profession as an assassin.
